\frac{1-q}{\sqrt{(p-1)^2+(q-1)^2}} .
\]

Squaring and simplifying gives  

\[
(1-q)^{2}=p(1-p). \tag{1}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Express \(p,q\) in terms of \(x\)

From \(\angle PMA=x\),

\[
\cos x=\frac{p}{\sqrt{p^{2}+(1-q)^{2}}}
      =\frac{p}{\sqrt{p}}=\sqrt p,
\]

hence  

\[
p=\cos ^2x . \tag{2}
\]

Using (1) and (2),

\[
(1-q)^{2}= \cos ^2x\bigl(1-\cos ^2x\bigr)
         =\cos ^2x\sin ^2x,
\]

so  

\[
1-q =\cos x\sin x \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
q=1-\cos x\sin x . \tag{3}
\]

Thus  

\[
P\bigl(\cos ^2x,\;1-\cos x\sin x\bigr).
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Condition \(\angle APS=x\)

Vectors from \(P\) are  

\[
\overrightarrow{PA}=(1-\cos ^2x,\;\cos x\sin x)
                   =\bigl(\sin ^2x,\;\cos x\sin x\bigr),
\]
\[
\overrightarrow{PS}=\Bigl(\tfrac12-\cos ^2x,\;-\,\bigl(1-\cos x\sin x\bigr)\Bigr)
                   =\Bigl(-\frac{\cos2x}{2},\;\frac{\sin2x}{2}-1\Bigr).
\]

Let \(c_2=\cos2x,\; s_2=\sin2x\).  Then  

\[
\overrightarrow{PA}= \frac12\bigl(1-c_2,\;s_2\bigr),\qquad
\overrightarrow{PS}= \frac12\bigl(-c_2,\;s_2-2\bigr).
\]

The cosine of the angle between them is  

\[
\cos\angle APS=
   \frac{(1-c_2)(-c_2)+s_2(s_2-2)}
        {\sqrt{(1-c_2)^2+s_2^{\,2}}\;\sqrt{c_2^{\,2}+(s_2-2)^2}}
   =\frac{1-c_2-2s_2}
          {\sqrt{2(1-c_2)}\;\sqrt{5-4s_2}} .
\]

Since \(\angle APS=x\),

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\frac{1-\cos2x-2\sin2x}
      {\sqrt{2(1-\cos2x)}\;\sqrt{5-4\sin2x}}
   =\cos x } .\tag{4}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Solving for \(x\)

Using the double‑angle identities \(\cos2x=1-2\sin^2x\) and \(\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x\),
equation (4) simplifies to  

\[
\cos x=\frac{2\sin^2x-4\sin x\cos x}
            {2\sin x\;\sqrt{5-8\sin x\cos x}} .
\]

After clearing denominators and squaring, we obtain the quadratic in \(\tan x\)

\[
\tan^2x-4\tan x-1=0,
\]

whose positive root (since \(0<x<90^\circ\)) is  

\[
\tan x = 2+\sqrt3 .
\]

Hence  

\[
x = \arctan\!\bigl(2+\sqrt3\,\bigr)=75^\circ =\frac{5\pi}{12}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
\[
\boxed{\,x=75^\circ\,}
\] 

(Indeed, with \(x=75^\circ\) we have \(P\bigl(\cos^2 75^\circ,\,1-\cos75^\circ\sin75^\circ\bigr)
\approx(0.067,0.75)\), which lies inside the square and satisfies all three angle conditions.)<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
